lead: The first law balances energy but cannot fix the direction of flow. The second law does, in two equivalent forms. Kelvin-Planck speaks of engines; Clausius speaks of refrigerators. Each forbids one impossible machine. Engineers use them to reject impossible claims and to set plant efficiency limits.
prereq: You need 3.1 for engine and refrigerator pictures; Unit 2 for energy balance.

sections.h3: Kelvin-Planck: no engine on one reservoir

blocks.text: An engine takes heat Q₁ from a hot reservoir at T₁, rejects Q₂ to a cold reservoir at T₂, and gives work W = Q₁ − Q₂.

blocks.where: η is thermal efficiency; W is net work per cycle in kJ; Q₁ and Q₂ are heat taken and rejected per cycle in kJ.

blocks.text: Kelvin-Planck statement: it is impossible for any device working in a cycle to receive heat from a single reservoir and produce net work.
In a cycle means it returns to its starting state. Single reservoir means no other body. Then Q₂ = 0 and η = 100%. Such a machine is a perpetual motion machine of the second kind, PMM2.
A PMM2 obeys the first law: 1000 kJ in, 1000 kJ out. It breaks direction. A ship could run on sea heat. Real engines reject heat: a coal plant to a river, a car through its radiator.

sections.h3: Clausius: heat does not climb by itself

blocks.text: A refrigerator runs backwards: takes Q₂ from a cold body at T₂, receives work W, delivers Q₁ = Q₂ + W to a hot body at T₁.
Clausius statement: it is impossible to construct a device working in a cycle whose only effect is to transfer heat from a lower temperature to a higher temperature.

Only effect carries the weight: no work, no fuel, no change in device or surroundings. Refrigeration is not forbidden. A kitchen fridge moves heat from 4 °C to 35 °C using wall-socket work. Hot tea cools and never heats itself; a sealed box that chills inside and warms the room with no plug violates Clausius.

sections.h3: The two statements are one law

blocks.text: Neither follows from the first law; each is a postulate. Accepting one forces the other. Both proofs use contradiction.

Assume a PMM2, break Clausius. A 100% engine takes Q from T₁ and gives W = Q, rejecting nothing. Drive a reversible refrigerator between T₁ and colder T₂: it removes Q₂ from T₂ and delivers Q₂ + W to T₁. Hot reservoir loses Q, gains Q₂ + Q, net gain Q₂. Cold body loses Q₂. Work in equals work out. Heat Q₂ has climbed cold to hot with no work input — Clausius broken.

Assume a free refrigerator, break Kelvin-Planck. A device lifts Q₂ from T₂ to T₁ with no work. Run an engine between the same bodies: takes Q₁ from T₁, gives W = Q₁ − Q₂, rejects Q₂ to T₂. The free device carries Q₂ back up. Hot loses Q₁ − Q₂ = W, cold unchanged, W work appears. A cycle made work from one reservoir — a PMM2.
Both directions hold; the statements stand or fall together.

items: Heat crosses a temperature difference from hot to cold only unless work is spent.
A cycle on one reservoir cannot produce net work: no engine has η = 100%.
No real engine reaches 100%; 3.4 gives the limit for a given pair.
A real refrigerator needs work, so COP = Q₂/W is finite.

figure.caption: The 100% engine takes 200 kJ from the 300 K body and gives 200 kJ work; that drives a reversible refrigerator that removes 300 kJ from the same body and dumps 500 kJ into 500 K. Net: 500 kJ climbs from 300 K to 500 K with zero work input. Clausius forbids this. Numbers match the example.

spec.title: How one violation creates the other
spec.aria: A 100% efficient engine takes 200 kJ from a 300 K body and makes 200 kJ of work, which drives a reversible refrigerator of COP 1.5; the pair moves 500 kJ from 300 K to 500 K with no work input and no other change.

examples.question: An inventor claims an engine that takes 1000 kJ from a reservoir at 500 K, rejects 400 kJ to a reservoir at 300 K, and delivers 600 kJ of work. (a) Check the claim against the first law and against a reversible engine between the same two reservoirs. (b) Combine the claim with a reversed reversible engine to show it violates the Kelvin-Planck statement. (c) Use the excess work in a reversible refrigerator to show it violates the Clausius statement too.
steps: First law: W = 1000 − 400 = 600 kJ. Claim matches; first law accepts it.
Reversible engine: η_rev = 1 − 300/500 = 40%. With Q₁ = 1000 kJ, W_rev = 400 kJ, Q₂_rev = 600 kJ.
Reverse the reversible engine: driven by 400 kJ, it removes 600 kJ from 300 K and delivers 1000 kJ to 500 K.
Combine. Hot reservoir: −1000 + 1000 = 0. Cold body: +400 − 600 = −200 kJ, so 200 kJ leaves. Work: 600 − 400 = 200 kJ net out.
This cyclic pair takes 200 kJ from one 300 K reservoir and makes 200 kJ work. PMM2; Kelvin-Planck violated. First law still balances.
Spend 200 kJ in a reversible refrigerator between 500 K and 300 K. COP = 300/(500 − 300) = 1.5. It removes 300 kJ from 300 K and delivers 500 kJ to 500 K.
Add to step 7: cold body loses 200 + 300 = 500 kJ; 500 K reservoir gains 500 kJ; work in equals work out. Heat climbs 300 K to 500 K with no work input: Clausius violated.
examples.answer: The claim obeys the first law but gives 200 kJ extra work; combined with reversible devices it moves 500 kJ from 300 K to 500 K with zero work input, breaking both statements.
examples.check:
T1, T2 = 500.0, 300.0
Q1, Q2, W = 1000.0, 400.0, 600.0
print(round(Q1 - Q2, 4))
eta_claim = W / Q1
print(round(eta_claim, 4))
eta_rev = 1 - T2 / T1
print(round(eta_rev, 4))
W_rev = eta_rev * Q1
print(round(W_rev, 4))
Q2_rev = Q1 - W_rev
print(round(Q2_rev, 4))
W_extra = W - W_rev
print(round(W_extra, 4))
Q_cold = Q2_rev - Q2
print(round(Q_cold, 4))
COP = T2 / (T1 - T2)
print(round(COP, 4))
Q2_f = COP * W_extra
print(round(Q2_f, 4))
Q1_f = Q2_f + W_extra
print(round(Q1_f, 4))
print(round(Q_cold + Q2_f, 4))

traps: Kelvin-Planck is about a cyclic device, not one process. Isothermal expansion of an ideal gas is legal; repeating it needs compression work.
The statements are one law in two forms. A violation of one violates the other.
A PMM2 obeys conservation of energy. It breaks direction. Calling it a first-law violation is wrong; that is PMM1.
Clausius does not ban refrigerators. It bans heat uphill with no work and no other change.
For a reversible refrigerator, COP = T₂/(T₁ − T₂); cold temperature on top.

quiz.a: It is impossible for any device working in a cycle to receive heat from a single reservoir and produce net work.
It is impossible to construct a device working in a cycle whose only effect is to transfer heat from a lower temperature to a higher temperature.

quiz.q: Why does a perpetual motion machine of the second kind not violate the first law?
quiz.a: Energy balance W = Q₁: 1000 kJ in, 1000 kJ out. The first law only counts energy. PMM2 breaks the direction rule, the second law.

quiz.q: An ideal gas in a cylinder expands isothermally and converts 50 kJ of heat into 50 kJ of work. Does this break the Kelvin-Planck statement?
quiz.a: No. Kelvin-Planck speaks of a device in a cycle. One expansion is not a cycle. To repeat it, compress the gas back; that needs work, so no net work.

quiz.q: A claimed engine takes 900 kJ from a reservoir at 600 K and rejects 300 kJ to a reservoir at 300 K. A reversible engine between the same reservoirs would take the same 900 kJ and reject 450 kJ. Find the claimed efficiency, the reversible efficiency, and the excess work.
Using the numbers of the previous question, show that the claim combined with a reversed reversible engine gives work from a single reservoir.
quiz.a: Drive reversed reversible engine with 450 kJ: takes 450 kJ from 300 K, delivers 900 kJ to 600 K. Add claim: hot loses 900, gains 900, net zero. Cold gains 300, loses 450, net loss 150 kJ. Work out = 600 − 450 = 150 kJ. A cycle takes 150 kJ from one 300 K reservoir and makes work: PMM2, Kelvin-Planck violated.

quiz.q: A sealed box chills its inside and warms the room with no power supply, no fuel, and runs for years. Which statement does it break? If the Kelvin-Planck statement were false, could such a box exist?
quiz.a: It breaks Clausius: only effect is heat from cold to hot. If PMM2 existed, it could drive a reversible refrigerator; the pair would move heat uphill with no work input. So yes, the box could exist, which is why the statements stand together.

beyond: Not for exam. These statements seed exergy analysis in Unit 4, where how much heat could become work gets a number from the dead-state temperature. Maxwell's demon and Landauer's principle: erasing one bit costs at least kT ln2 of work, so no demon runs free. Same accounting sets data-centre power bills and heat-pump limits. Searches: perpetual motion machine of the second kind, Landauer's principle, second law efficiency.
